text:
Priya S.: Heads up — spotted a canary rollout executed by a service account that shouldn't have rollout privileges. Suspect RBAC change from last week's policy refactor. Anyone else see this?

Jonah R.: Which service account? can you paste the audit id?

Priya S.: svc-dataflow-agg. Audit log id: audit-2025-03-10-0812-77. From the logs it called /rollout/v1/execute. Filtered snippet: ```
INFO service=rollout user=svc-dataflow-agg action=rollout.execute target=canary/blue-42 trace=tx-9f3a status=200
```

Lina M.: @Priya S. that SA should only have `models.read` + `kv.write` per role-mappings. Where did it pick up `rollout.execute`?

Priya S.: Looks like rbac-policy v3 merged Friday — policy id `rbac-v3-2025-03-07`. The PR added wildcard to ops actions: `actions: ['ops.*']` for group `platform-ops`. Maybe service account was indirectly in platform-ops via group sync.

Jonah R.: Oof. Is group sync to LDAP adding svc-dataflow-agg? @Lina can you check membership mapping? Also we need to know if KMS keys were used for signing the rollout request (we sign canary requests to prevent replay).

Lina M.: Checking now. Group mapping shows svc-dataflow-agg is in `dataflow-hosts` and `platform-ops` via AD nested group `automation-service-accounts`. Looks like nested groups were flattened in the v3 change.

security-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-20250310-23 - potential permission escalation allowing canary rollouts outside intended principals. Assigned: sec-team, oncall: @jonah

Priya S.: We need audit trail + KMS key usage. @devops can you pull key usage for `kms-rollout-signing` between 2025-03-07 and now? If the SA used the key that's more serious.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: canary deploy blue-42 triggered by user svc-dataflow-agg at 2025-03-10T08:12:20Z. Signature validated using KMS key `projects/redwood/keys/kms-rollout-signing`.

Jonah R.: So key was used. That implies SA had signing permission too. Two problems: group flattening + KMS IAM. Open question: did the v3 policy inadvertently grant KMS sign permission or did KMS role mapping include platform-ops?

Lina M.: KMS IAM currently grants `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to group `automation-kms-users`. That group maps to the same nested AD group. v3 policy flattened nested groups and also triggered a sync of `automation-kms-users` into `platform-ops` service role. I'll attach lines from policy change.

Priya S.: We should rollback the wildcard change and add explicit deny for `rollout.execute` to service accounts. Also need to add audit log alert for any non-human principal calling `rollout.execute`.

Jonah R.: Agreed. Proposed immediate steps: 1) Temporarily revoke `platform-ops` membership for nested automation groups; 2) Roll back rbac-policy v3 wildcard; 3) Rotate `kms-rollout-signing` key to block reuse; 4) Postmortem + add unit tests for group flattening.

Lina M.: I'll do #1 and #2 now. FYI will cause some scheduled jobs to fail; will notify infra teams.

Priya S.: :thumbsup: Please also add a short retention window query for audit logs — we need to export the raw request payloads for the investigation (retain 90 days in secure bucket).

Jonah R.: Assigned follow-ups: sec-ticket #4527 (investigation), infra-change #987 (rollback), kms-rotation #988. I'll own the postmortem.

Priya S.: Thanks. If anyone finds other SAs with `rollout.execute`, drop them here. I'll DM legal for disclosure guidance.
